newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses firm, dollar/Europe plays reign.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses firm, dollar/Europe plays reign.

text.p: The mark was firmer on its European cross rates despite setting new 7-1/2 year lows against the dollar early Monday and traders said dollar strength against all European currencies was the central focus.
The dollar set its highest level against the mark since October 1989 and near multi-year peaks against a host of European currencies including the Swiss and French francs and the lira.
This was helping the mark gain somewhat against its European counterparts, but moves on the crosses were generally small.
"On the whole, the mark's become neutral against the European crosses at the moment," said Masahiro Kawasaki, manager at Sakura Bank in London.

"It would be understandable for it to be a bit weaker on the crosses (considering the mark's weakness against the majors), but at the same time the other European currencies are all losing against the dollar because of economic fundamentals and the EMU issue," Kawasaki said.
The mark was at 3.3715/20 French francs at 0915 GMT against its late Friday European level of 3.3707/12, while against the Swiss franc it was at 82.08/10 centimes against 81.84/87.

Traders said they were loath to push the mark decisively in either direction for now until they saw the German Bundesbank's and Bank of England's decisions regarding key interest rates later this week.

The BoE's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet on Wednesday and Thursday with the market seeing a possible rise in the base rate, which would be Britain's fourth such rate hike in as many months.
But the key for the mark would be the Bundesbank's decision on its securities repurchase money market rate, which could be changed as early as this week, analysts said.
